candidates.title: Web Summit Lisbon 2026 opens with Chinese robots on stage and a message: the next superstars come from China
candidates.summary: Web Summit 2026 opened on the evening of 9 November at the MEO Arena with Agibot's robots as the opening act. Paddy Cosgrave told the audience that the tech superstars of the future come from China rather than California, called this the most international edition yet (164 countries, every European country) and said it has the largest number of Portuguese startups ever. Lisbon's mayor Carlos Moedas spoke on the city's tech jobs and the unicorns that opened offices there.
candidates.why_it_matters: The summit's own framing for 2026 is a US-China AI race with Europe and Portugal in the middle; that is the context every company story this week sits in, and the Portuguese startups claim is a figure our readers will want checked.

quote.text: The superstars of the future are not coming from California; they're coming from China.
quote.by: Paddy Cosgrave, Web Summit CEO, opening night

claims_to_check: 164 countries (reported by Jornal Económico); 'largest ever number of Portuguese startups' (reported by Euronews and Jornal Económico, no figure given): to be checked against Web Summit's own press release
Also on stage, reported by Euronews: Cloudflare's Matthew Prince on Nvidia's probe of Jensen Huang, and Manus's co-founder Tao Zhang on hiring people who work with AI (agents beat)
